content: Before taking benzphetamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other sympathomimetic amines (such as decongestants like pseudoephedrine, stimulants like amphetamine, or appetite suppressants like phentermine), or if you have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Benzphetamine may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. This medication should not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. If you become pregnant or suspect you might be pregnant, notify your doctor immediately. Infants born to mothers who have used this medication for a prolonged period or in high doses may experience withdrawal symptoms, such as irritability or extreme fatigue. Benzphetamine may pass into breast milk and could have undesirable effects on a nursing infant; therefore, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Taking benzphetamine with monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors (such as isocarboxazid, phenelzine, or tranylcypromine) can result in a serious, potentially fatal drug interaction. Avoid using MAO inhibitors during treatment with benzphetamine and for two weeks before starting this medication. If someone overdoses and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Do not share this medication with others. Appetite suppressants should not replace a proper diet. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose or late in the evening, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
